sources.label: Waverley Council lifeguards, 100 years - The Beast

blocks.text: The thing people can't quite believe about Bondi Rescue is that none of it is acting. The lifeguards you see are genuine Waverley Council employees doing a real job - the cameras just follow them around. Here are 20 things I love telling visitors about the show that turned my local beach into one of the most-watched stretches of sand on earth.

items: 1. It premiered on 15 February 2006 on Network Ten - nearly two decades on, that makes it one of the longest-running factual series Australia has produced.
2. It wasn't a broadcaster's idea. It was created by Ben Davies, a part-time Bondi lifeguard, together with documentary-maker Michael Cordell - the first crew were filming their own workmates.
3. It's made by Cordell Jigsaw Productions, the house behind a long run of Australian documentary hits.
4. The narration is by Osher Günsberg - the presenter many older viewers still remember as 'Andrew G'.
5. It's a serious awards magnet: it won the Logie for Most Popular Factual Program six years running, from 2008 to 2013.
6. By its 2024 run it had reached 18 seasons and more than 200 episodes - a remarkable innings for any unscripted show.
7. It screens in dozens of countries, which is why I regularly meet visitors who came to Bondi because of the telly.

blocks.text: The lifeguards behind the tank tops

items: 8. They're genuine Waverley Council employees. The council has paid professionals to watch this beach since 1913, when it hired its first full-time lifeguard - the show simply points a camera at a job that's more than a century old.
9. The same service also patrols neighbouring Tamarama and Bronte, and works all three beaches 365 days a year - their patch stretches well beyond the famous crescent.
10. Head lifeguard Bruce 'Hoppo' Hopkins has led the team since 2000 and been a Bondi lifeguard since 1991; he was named Australian Lifeguard of the Year in 2006, the show's very first year.
11. The nicknames are a whole culture in themselves - Harries, Deano, Whippet, Maxi, Chappo - and most of them predate the cameras.
12. They're qualified professionals holding lifeguard and first-aid tickets; the drama on screen is their ordinary shift.
13. Across a busy summer the Bondi team logs thousands of rescues - far more than any season could show, so only a fraction ever makes it to air.

blocks.text: Want to see the show in real life? The lifeguards run training drills on the sand at quieter times. Watch from the promenade near the tower at the south end rather than crowding the flagged swimming area - that space needs to stay clear for real patrols.
The stuff the camera doesn't dwell on

items: 14. The number-one hazard on the show isn't sharks - it's rip currents, the fast channels of water that pull swimmers out to sea.
15. A huge share of rescues involve visitors who simply don't recognise a rip - exactly why the show keeps hammering the flags.
16. 'Swim between the red-and-yellow flags' isn't a catchphrase; it's the single most useful thing the series has taught millions of viewers.
17. It's observational documentary, not scripted reality - there's no writers' room deciding who nearly drowns on Saturday.
18. The weather you rarely see is a big part of the job: the lifeguards work grey, wild and freezing days that never make glossy TV.
19. The fame is real - Bondi's lifeguards get stopped for photos around the world.
20. For all the drama, the show has probably saved lives off-screen too, by teaching people to respect the surf before they swim.

blocks.title: Watch the show, but respect the water
blocks.text: Bondi is a patrolled beach with real rips. No amount of watching Bondi Rescue replaces the basics: always swim between the red-and-yellow flags, never swim alone, and if you're caught in a rip, stay calm, raise an arm and let the current carry you while you signal for help.

items.q: Is Bondi Rescue scripted or real?
items.a: It's real. The lifeguards are actual Waverley Council professionals doing their day job, and the show is an observational documentary - the crews follow genuine patrols and rescues rather than a script.

items.q: Can I meet the Bondi Rescue lifeguards?
items.a: Sometimes - they're often on patrol from the tower at the south end of the beach. Please don't distract them while they're watching the water; if you'd like a photo, wait until they're clearly on a break.

items.q: Which beaches do the Bondi lifeguards actually cover?
items.a: The service is centred on Bondi but also patrols the neighbouring beaches of Tamarama and Bronte, keeping watch across all three 365 days a year.

blocks.text: The best 'fact', though, is one you can test yourself: come down, swim between the flags, and you'll soon see why this beach earned its own TV show.
